reviews.title: ĐÀM NGUYỄN LÂM NHI · IELTS 49 · W07 · Đề 1
reviews.overall: Em đọc đúng đề, ghi đúng số liệu và nêu được Argentina tăng, Australia giảm, Thailand luôn đứng đầu. Tuy nhiên, câu mở bài đặt tên ba nước giữa “cars” và “were made” nên khó đọc; em cần sắp lại. Overview còn thiếu việc Thailand đạt đỉnh năm 2006 rồi giảm. Trong Detail, “constant growth” chưa có căn cứ, chủ ngữ của hai câu tăng giảm chưa đúng, và “expenenced” sai chính tả. Cô yêu cầu em sửa các chỗ này rồi nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em chia Detail 1 cho Thailand và Australia, Detail 2 cho Argentina; cách chia theo nước vẫn có thể dùng vì em đã nêu các mốc của từng nước. Tuy nhiên, nhãn “categories with rising figures” ở Detail 2 không khớp với nội dung chỉ nói về Argentina, còn câu cuối lặp lại xu hướng Australia đã mô tả. Cô gợi ý dùng năm 2006 để chia hai giai đoạn, nhờ đó em trình bày rõ lúc Argentina vượt Australia và lúc Thailand bắt đầu giảm.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given table illustrates how many cars in 3 different countries - namely Argentina, Australia, Thailand were made in 2003, 2006, and 2009.

Overall, there was a general increase in the number of cars made in Argentina. By contrast, Australia experienced a progressive decline. Also of note is that Thailand consistently had the highest figures throughout the years.

To elaborate, in 2003, 735,852 cars were made in Thailand with a constant growth to 1,162,356 in 2006, marking the highest point of the entire table before it slightly fell to 999,963 in 2009. However, the number of cars made in Australia was 452,163 in 2003, followed by a gradual decrease to 341,268 in 2006 and a final drop to 245,624 in 2009. These figures, conversely, always went down over the whole timescale.

Regarding the categories with rising figures, Argentina started at 235,088 cars, after which it expenenced an upturn to 352,759 in 2006 and continued to rise to 466,089 in 2009. The opposite pattern, however, was seen in Australia.

From 2006 to 2009, the number of cars made in Thailand decreased to 999,963 but remained higher than the figures for the other two countries. The figure for Argentina continued to rise, reaching 466,089 cars in 2009. By contrast, Australian production dropped again to 245,624, making it the lowest of the three that year.

The given line chart illustrates the prison population in a European country over a period of 90 years, commencing from 1911.

Overall, there was an increase in the number of male prisoners in European country, while an opposite trend was observed in the case of female prisoners. Also of note is that, male prisoners consistently had the highest figures throughout the years.

To elaborate, in 1911, around 3,000 female imprisoned for the crimes with a significant fall to 500 people in 1941, making the lowest point of the entire graph. The figures for male prisoners, similarly, decline from nearly 20,000 people to 10,000 during the same period of time.

Regarding the latter half of the provided time line, the number of male and female prisoners has been recorded as having increased. In 1951, 20,000 males became prisoners, with a subsequent considerable rise to 40,000 people in 1981 and a constant growth to almost 50,000 prisoners in 2001, reaching the highest figure on the chart. A growth was, likewise recorded in the figures for female prisoners, yet less noticeable, of a 1,000 people from 1951 to 1961. Finally, the female prisoners remained unchanged at 2,000 people in 2001. All in all, the whole period, the number of male prisoners was always higher than that of female prisoners.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The two line charts compare the numbers of male and female prisoners in a European country between 1911 and 2001.

Overall, the male prison population was consistently much larger than the female one. The number of male prisoners declined at first but rose substantially later, especially from 1971 to 1981. By contrast, the female figure fell sharply to an early low, fluctuated afterwards and ended below its initial level.

In 1911, there were about 18,000 male prisoners, and the figure remained similar in 1921. It then dropped to approximately 10,000 in 1931 before recovering to nearly 20,000 by 1951. After staying close to this level until 1971, the male total jumped to around 39,000 in 1981, followed by a further rise to approximately 46,000 in 2001.

The female prison population started at about 3,200 in 1911 and fell to its lowest level, around 500, in 1941. It recovered to roughly 1,500 by 1961 but dropped again to about 700 in 1971. The figure subsequently rose to around 1,600 in 1991 and almost 2,000 by 2001, still well below its starting point.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line chart illustrates the amount of fish and 4 different kinds of meat consumed per person per week in a European country over a 25-year period, commencing from 1979.

Overall, there was a general decrease in the amount of beef, lamb and fish consumed, while an opposite trend was observed in the case of chicken. Also of note is that fish consumption consistently had the lowest figures throughout the years.

To elaborate, in 1979, 220 grams of beef was consumed, with a slightly grow to 240 in 1984 but latterly fell to 200 grams in 1989 and more significant decline to 100 grams in 2004. A downturn was, likewise, recorded in the figures for lamb, with a general decline to 150 gram in 1979 and sharp drop to 50 grams in 2004.

Regarding the categories with different trend, the intake of fish also decline but virtually unchanged, falling from 55 grams per person per week in 1979 to 50 grams in 1984 and finally fell to 48 grams in 2004. However, the figures for chicken went up nearly 150 grams in 1979 to 200 grams in 1989 and kept rising to 250 grams in 2004, marking the highest point of the entire graph.

Overall, there was a general increase in the proportion of young people with higher education in A, C and D. While there was a stable period in the figures for B. Also of note is that D consistently had the highest figures throughout the years.

Regarding categories with lower data, the share of young people in higher education in C also went up, yet less noticeable of a mere 1%, from 50% in 2000 to 51% and 52% in 2005 and 2010. Meanwhile, the figures for B remained unchanged at 40% in 2000 and 2010. This proportion even dropped by 1% in 2005. These data almost the lowest figures over the whole timescale.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given pie charts illustrate the proportions of reasons why students chose a particular university in the UK over a 10-year period, commencing from 1997.

Overall, the percentage of student’s demand about suitable degree courses, proximity to parent house and quality of teaching generally increased, while the opposite was true for quality of resources and good sports and social activities. Notably, suitable degree courses consistently recorded higher figures than other reasons throughout the years.

To elaborate, the highest share of the reasons why students chose a university was suitable degree courses, which they accounted for almost a third of the total. Beside that, the proportion of students choosing a university close to their parent’s houses also significantly went up from 10% in 1997 to 22% in 2007, and the figure for teaching quality also rose by 3% in the same time.

Regarding categories with the declined data, students placed less emphasis on the quality of resources when it fell from 21% in 1997 to 17% in 2007, likewise, the figures for good sport and social activities decreased substantially from 19% to 6%, marking the least reasons why student chose a university in 2007.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The given pie charts illustrate how the proportions of students choosing a particular university in the UK for different reasons changed between 1997 and 2007.

Overall, the proportions of students citing suitable degree courses, proximity to their parents’ homes and teaching quality increased, whereas the shares for resource quality and good sports and social activities declined. Suitable courses remained the leading reason in both years. Proximity to home saw the largest rise, while sports and social activities became the least cited reason in 2007.

To elaborate, in 1997, 35% of students selected the university for its suitable degree courses, with a slight rise to 37% in 2007; this was the highest share in both years. The figure for proximity to their parents’ homes grew much more sharply, from 10% to 22%, while that for teaching quality increased by three percentage points, from 15% to 18%.

Regarding the two reasons that declined, the proportion choosing the university for its resources fell from 21% in 1997 to 17% in 2007. Likewise, the figure for good sports and social activities dropped from 19% to 6% over the same period, a fall of 13 percentage points and the sharpest decline among the reasons.
